finding: The previous image painter normalized the pixel axes and built an orthogonal rotation/mirror transform. For a skewed U/V basis, clipped pixel rendering did not align with the image geometry and hit testing.
change: Use the full U and V vectors transformed into viewport coordinates to form one affine pixel-to-viewport transform. The same painter path handles normal and inverted clipping and unclipped images; the previous smooth-pixmap rendering hint is retained.
checks: A locally generated skewed-axis clipping test failed eight assertions on the prior painter and passes with the corrected transform.

The final bundled-codec Qt offscreen image selection passes 1064 assertions across seven axis bases, normal and inverted rectangular/polygon clipping, disabled clipping, and entity copies. A colored raster checks image orientation for orthogonal, rotated, skewed, and mirrored-skewed axes, both with and without a rotated/translated UCS.
The current system-codec build passes the 3425-assertion selected large-polygon IMAGE graph and guarded-save control.

On macOS ARM64, the current consumer rendered a locally generated 18-vertex clipped IMAGE with U=(1,0) and V=(0.5,1); its skewed appearance remained after Save As and reopen. Independent ezdxf checked matching pixel vectors, all clipping vertices, image/definition/reactor graph and clean audits for source and output. The scratch app used an isolated settings organization and a separate signed bundle. No drawing fixture was committed.
limits: Selected synthetic 2D image bases on macOS ARM64; native GUI covers one skewed image. Printing, extreme coordinates, nonplanar geometry, other producers, Linux and Windows remain unqualified.
Existing bounded source/graph and more-than-256-vertex restrictions still apply.
